The places represented were as in Strafford’s time, but no doubt care was taken that the assembly should be entirely Protestant. Sir James Barry, afterwards Lord Santry, was chosen Speaker, and William Temple sat for the county of Carlow. The Council of State ordered the convention to dissolve, but this they refused, while repudiating any idea of separation from England. Sir Hardress Waller had hitherto gone with the rest; but it became evident that Royalism was winning, and he had sat regularly as one of the late King’s judges, and signed his death-warrant. He made himself master of the Castle, and it was believed that he intended to seize Coote and other leaders who had declared in print for a free Parliament and the readmission of all the secluded members. The convention had the power of the purse, and the soldiers in the Castle, who were probably tired of barrack-revolutions and deferred pay, surrendered Waller and the few officers who supported him. Coote sent Sir Arthur Forbes, a noted Royalist who had been with Montrose, to Brussels with an offer of his services, and Charles gladly accepted them, offering an earldom and other benefits, and proposing to join him, ‘except it be more necessary that I go\[Pg 370\] for England.’ Broghill sent his brother Francis, afterwards Lord Shannon, about the same time; and, if we are to believe his not very trustworthy biographer, Charles was on the point of starting for Ireland by way of Calais when he heard that things were going so well in England as to make the journey unnecessary. What is more certain is that Broghill was at Cork three days after Waller’s attempt, and there, at the head of the Munster officers, signed a declaration in favour of a full and free Parliament, and of readmitting the members ousted by Pride’s Purge. All men, they said, were tired of anarchy and of authorities constantly changing, and for the moment there was no safety but in restoring the Long Parliament to its unpurged condition. ‘If the excluded members be readmitted, they must be either the greater or the lesser number in the House; if the lesser, where is the danger of their admission? If the greater, where is the justice of their exclusion? For then it will appear that the minor number keeps out the major.’ Whatever may have been Broghill’s secret negotiations, he kept up a correspondence with Thurloe long after Monck had come to Whitehall, and repudiated the idea of bringing in the King as late as April 24. Even on May 8, when Charles was proclaimed in London, he still talked of preserving ‘the just rights we contended for so successfully in the war,’ very truly observing that if no conditions were made before the then inevitable restoration, it would be next to impossible to make any afterwards.[\[305\]](https://www.gutenberg.org/files/53916/53916-h/53916-h.htm#Footnote_305_305) Charles II. proclaimed in Dublin, May 14. Coote and Broghill Lords Justices. According to his biographer and chaplain, Broghill was the moving spirit, and Coote acted under his influence; but\[Pg 371\] this is extremely doubtful. Broghill loved tortuous ways, and was perhaps anxious to leave himself a loophole in any case. Foreseeing the importance of the Convention Parliament in England, he was most anxious to be in it, and, having married a Howard, he found a seat at Arundel. Coote and his friends were ready to declare themselves before decisive steps were taken in London, but it was felt that the restored King might be embarrassed by premature action, and means were taken to delay proceedings. Charles II. was not proclaimed in Dublin till May 14, and on the 25th Broghill was sent with Coote and others to attend the King. Whatever those in all the secrets may have thought, Coote was at first much better received by the Royalists generally, who looked upon his colleague and rival as a trimmer. Three days later the Irish Convention adjourned till November. Monck was appointed Lord Lieutenant and Lord Roberts Deputy; but neither of them came over, and at the end of the year Sir Maurice Eustace, who had been made Lord Chancellor, was appointed Lord Justice, with Coote and Broghill as colleagues. The two soldiers were treated as of equal importance, the one being made Earl of Orrery on September 5, and the other Earl of Mountrath on the following 48.content:
August 1640: The Second Bishops' War. The English "New Army" under the Earl of Stafford is pushed back through Northumberland and the [Scots](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usscotfax/society/scottish.html) under [Alexander Leslie](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/l/alexanderleslie.html) take Newcastle on 28 August. Meanwhile the Covenanters take both [Edinburgh](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/edinburgh/edinburghcastle/index.html) and [Dumbarton](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/dumbarton/dumbartoncastle/index.html) castles; and the Duke of Argyll attacks the royalist clans in the Highlands.

12 September 1640: The death in London of [Sir William Alexander,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/a/williamalexander.html) 1st Earl of Stirling, the Royal courtier and poet who established Nova Scotia.

26 October 1640: Hostilities cease with a truce signed at Ripon, under which [Charles I](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesi.html) agrees to pay the costs of keeping their army in northern England.

3 November 1640: [King Charles I](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesi.html) convenes the English Parliament to raise the funds to settle with the [Scots](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usscotfax/society/scottish.html) as agreed at Ripon. This "Long Parliament" will to sit until 1653 and lead to [Charles'](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesi.html) loss of his throne and his head.

14 August 1641: [Charles I](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesi.html) visits [Edinburgh](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/edinburgh/edinburgh/index.html) in an effort to placate opposition and buy off critics. He ends up confirming the decisions of the 1640 Free Parliament, and so, indirectly, the Covenant.

October 1641: The weakness of [Charles](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesi.html) in Scotland leads to Catholic revolt in Ulster, only suppressed with help from Protestant troops from Scotland.

22 August 1642: [Charles I,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesi.html) having failed to suppress or coerce the English Parliament by his will, takes it on by military might. The English Civil War begins.

17 August 1643: [Scotland](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usscotfax/society/scottish.html) offers to support the Parliamentary side in the Civil War in return for the acceptance by the English of a "Solemn League and Covenant", in effect exporting Presbyterianism to them. Military aspects are settled quickly and the English Parliament later accepts the religious aspects of the Covenant.

19 January 1644: A Scottish Covenanter army of 20,000 men under the command of [Alexander Leslie](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/l/alexanderleslie.html) moves south to support the Parliamentary Army.

February 1644: [King Charles](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesi.html) appoints the [Marquis of Montrose,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) who with other moderate Covenanters is now on the Royalist side, as head of Royalist forces in Scotland.

March 1644: [Montrose](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) captures [Dumfries](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/dumfries/dumfries/index.html) for the Royalists.

2 July 1644: The Parliamentary Army, reinforced by the Scottish Covenanters, defeat the Royalists at the Battle of Marston Moor.

August 1644: Alasdair MacDonald lands on the [Ardnamurchan Peninsula](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/kilchoan/ardnamurchanpoint/index.html) with 2000 troops from Ireland, who are quickly joined by a thousand highlanders. He supports the Royalist cause against Clan Campbell and storms through [Argyll](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usfeatures/areas/argyll.html) before joining forces with the [Marquis of Montrose](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) in Perthshire.

September 1644: MacDonald and [Montrose](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) defeat a large Covenanter force before taking [Perth.](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/perth/perth/index.html) They then take on and beat another larger force before taking and pillaging [Aberdeen](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/aberdeen/aberdeen/index.html) then retreating, pursued by the Marquis of Argyll.

13 September 1644: The Battle of Aberdeen between Royalists and Covenanters is followed by the sacking of [Aberdeen](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/aberdeen/aberdeen/index.html) by the victorious Royalist forces.

December 1644: [Montrose,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) supported by a reinforced Alasdair MacDonald, attacks [Inveraray](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/inveraray/inveraray/index.html) and the Campbell strongholds of [Argyll](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usfeatures/areas/argyll.html) killing a thousand Campbell Clansmen. They then withdraw north through the highland winter to [Inverlochy Castle,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/fortwilliam/inverlochy/index.html) near [Fort William.](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/fortwilliam/fortwilliam/index.html)

January 1645: [Montrose](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) heads towards [Inverness,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/inverness/inverness/index.html) only to find a Covenanter army is approaching from [Inverness.](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/inverness/inverness/index.html) Meanwhile, the Marquis of Argyll has followed him north, and reached [Inverlochy Castle.](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/fortwilliam/inverlochy/index.html)

2 February 1645: [The 1st Marquess of Montrose](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) makes a forced march south and surprises the Campbells at [Inverlochy Castle.](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/fortwilliam/inverlochy/index.html) Though outnumbered [Montrose](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) soundly defeats the Covenanters, killing 1,500 for the loss of far fewer men.

9 May 1645: The [Marquis of Montrose](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) and his Royalists camp at [Auldearn](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/auldearn/auldearn/index.html) near [Nairn,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/nairn/nairn/index.html) while en route to attack [Inverness.](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/inverness/inverness/index.html) The Covenanters, reinforced by troops withdrawn from England because of the threat from Montrose, gather at [Inverness](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/inverness/inverness/index.html) before marching overnight in an attempt to surprise Montrose at [Auldearn.](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/auldearn/auldearn/index.html) After a fierce fight the Royalists again win, killing 2,000 Covenanters for the loss of 200 of their own men.

14 June 1645: The New Model Army, with [Oliver Cromwell](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/c/olivercromwell.html) as its second-in-command, wins the decisive victory of the Civil War at Naseby.

2 July 1645: [The Marquis of Montrose](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) and the Royalists again defeat the Covenanters at the Battle of [Alford,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/alford/alford/index.html) in Aberdeenshire, but this time with considerable loss of life on both sides. [Montrose](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) has defeated the Covenanters throughout northern Scotland.

15 August 1645: At the Battle of [Kilsyth,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/kilsyth/kilsyth/index.html) midway between [Stirling](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/stirling/stirling/index.html) and [Glasgow,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/glasgow/glasgow/index.html) [Montrose](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) and the Royalists again defeat the Covenanters, killing 3,000. He moves on to capture [Glasgow](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/glasgow/glasgow/index.html) and [Edinburgh,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/edinburgh/edinburgh/index.html) effectively controlling Scotland.

13 September 1645: [Major-General Leslie's](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/l/davidleslie.html) Covenanter army returning from England after Naseby meets [Montrose](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) and the Royalists near [Selkirk](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/selkirk/selkirk/index.html) and comprehensively defeats them.

5 May 1646: [Charles I](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesi.html) surrenders to Scottish Covenanters besieging Newark on Trent. The Scots forces take him to Newcastle and try to bargain with him for Scots advantage. The English Parliamentary army threatens to take the King from the [Scots](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usscotfax/society/scottish.html) by force.

2 June 1646: [James Graham, 1st Marquess of Montrose](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) is ordered by [Charles I](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesi.html) to disband his forces and flee to France. He leaves the country in September.

19 August 1646: The death in [Edinburgh](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/edinburgh/edinburgh/index.html) of [Alexander Henderson](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/h/alexanderhenderson.html) the theologian closely involved in the drawing up of the 1638 National Covenant.

30 January 1647: The Scottish Covenanters march north and back to Scotland having handed [Charles I](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesi.html) over to the English in return for a payment of £200,000.

8 July 1648: The moderate arm of the Covenanters come to a secret agreement with [Charles I,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesi.html) now in English custody, and 20,000 [Scots](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usscotfax/society/scottish.html) move into England at the start of the Second Civil War.

17 August 1648: [Oliver Cromwell](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/c/olivercromwell.html) heavily defeats the Scots at Preston, leading to a return to power in [Edinburgh](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/edinburgh/edinburgh/index.html) of the radical Covenanters of the Kirk Party under the Marquis of Argyll.

4 October 1648: [Cromwell](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/c/olivercromwell.html) meets the Covenanters in [Edinburgh](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/edinburgh/edinburgh/index.html) leaving New Model Army troops to protect the hardline Presbyterians when he leaves.

30 January 1649: [Charles I](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesi.html) is executed in London despite protests from the Scots.

5 February 1649: The Scots Parliament proclaims [Charles II](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesii.html) as King.

March 1649: The English Parliament declares England to be a Republic.

March 1649: A delegation of Scots meets [Charles II](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesii.html) in the Hague demanding he impose Presbyterianism in Scotland, England and Ireland. Charles refuses.

March 1650: In a last effort to regain power by military means, [Charles II](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesii.html) seeks help from the [Marquis of Montrose,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) who lands in [Orkney](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/areaorkn/index.html) with 500 Scandinavian mercenaries before moving on to Caithness, reinforced by Orcadian volunteers.

27 April 1650: At the Battle of Carbisdale, near [Bonar Bridge,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/bonarbridge/bonarbridge/index.html) [James Graham, 1st Marquess of Montrose](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) is defeated with heavy losses by a much smaller Covenanter force under Colonel Strachan. [Montrose](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) escapes north-west until he is tricked into captivity at [Ardveck Castle,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/lochinver/ardvreckcastle/index.html) on the shore of Loch Assynt.

21 May 1650: The execution in [Edinburgh](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/edinburgh/edinburgh/index.html) of [James Graham, 1st Marquess of Montrose,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/g/jamesgrahammontrose.html) the influential Civil War military leader.

23 June 1650: [Charles II](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesii.html) lands at [Garmouth](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/garmouth/garmouth/index.html) in [Morayshire](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usfeatures/areas/moray.html) after sailing from the Netherlands and evading the English ships trying to intercept him. Charles signed the Covenant and the Solemn League immediately after coming ashore.

22 July 1650: [Oliver Cromwell](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/c/olivercromwell.html) invades Scotland and proceeds to the eastern edge of [Edinburgh.](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/edinburgh/edinburgh/index.html) The Scots form a defensive line within the city.

3 September 1650: The Battle of Dunbar is a resounding victory for [Cromwell,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/c/olivercromwell.html) largely because of the actions of extreme religious factions on the Scottish side. [Cromwell](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/c/olivercromwell.html) then marches on [Edinburgh](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/edinburgh/edinburgh/index.html) and subsequently occupies much of southern Scotland.

14 November 1650 (Gregorian calendar): The birth in the Netherlands of [William of Orange,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/williamiii.html) who became King William III of England and of Ireland on 22 January 1689, and King William II of Scotland on 4 April 1689.

1 January 1651: [Charles II](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesii.html) is crowned King of Scots at [Scone,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/perth/sconepalace/index.html) before touring those parts of Scotland not under English occupation.

July 1651: [Cromwell](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/c/olivercromwell.html) lands a force in [Fife](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usfeatures/areas/fife.html) that defeats the Scots at [Inverkeithing.](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/inverkeithing/inverkeithing/index.html) He then moves on to [Perth,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/perth/perth/index.html) tempting [Charles II](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesii.html) to use the gap he has left to advance on England and claim the throne. [Charles](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesii.html) takes the bait and [Cromwell](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/c/olivercromwell.html) follows.

14 August 1651: [General Monck,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/m/georgemonck.html) left by [Cromwell](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/c/olivercromwell.html) to complete the conquest of Scotland, takes [Stirling.](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/stirling/stirling/index.html)

22 August 1651: [Charles II](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesii.html) reaches Worcester with very little evidence of English Royalist support.

31 August 1651: A parliamentary army under the command of [General George Monck](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/m/georgemonck.html) attacks and takes [Broughty Castle.](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/broughty/broughtycastle/index.html)

1 September 1651: [General Monck](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/m/georgemonck.html) captures and pillages [Dundee.](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/dundee/dundee/index.html)

3 September 1651: [Cromwell](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/c/olivercromwell.html) attacks [Charles II](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesii.html) and the Scots Royalists defending Worcester and inflicts a heavy defeat on them. Charles Stewart manages to escape: many of the Scots including Major-General [David Leslie](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/l/davidleslie.html) do not.

15 October 1651: [Charles II](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/monarchs/charlesii.html) sails to France from Sussex after six weeks as a fugitive in England.

4 February 1652: [Cromwell's](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/c/olivercromwell.html) "Tender of Union" is announced in [Edinburgh.](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/edinburgh/edinburgh/index.html) This gives Scots 30 seats in a united Parliament in London. [General Monck](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/m/georgemonck.html) becomes Military Governor of Scotland and builds a series of defenses to ensure continued control over the country.

26 May 1652: The last Royalist stronghold anywhere on the eastern side of Scotland, [Dunnottar Castle](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/stonehaven/dunnottarcastle/index.html) near [Stonehaven,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/stonehaven/stonehaven/index.html) surrenders after an eight month siege, though not before the Scottish crown jewels have been smuggled out to safety in [Kinneff Old Church.](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/inverbervie/kinneffoldchurch/index.html)

July 1653: A General Assembly of the Kirk in [St Giles' Cathedral](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/edinburgh/stgiles/index.html) in [Edinburgh](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/edinburgh/edinburgh/index.html) is broken up by [Cromwell's](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/c/olivercromwell.html) troops.

16 December 1653: [Oliver Cromwell](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/c/olivercromwell.html) is sworn in as Lord Protector of England, Scotland, and Ireland.

19 July 1654: A Royalist uprising in the Highlands led by the Earl of Glencairn and [Major-General John Middleton](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/m/johnmiddleton.html) disintegrates after meeting troops under [General Monck](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/m/georgemonck.html) at the Battle of Dalnaspidal near Loch Garry.

23 November 1654: The birth in [Edinburgh](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/edinburgh/edinburgh/index.html) of [George Watson,](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/w/georgewatson.html) the account whose beqest allowed what is now George Watson's College to be founded.

1657: George Fox comes to Scotland as a missionary for the Quaker Society of Friends.

3 September 1658: [Oliver Cromwell](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usbiography/c/olivercromwell.html) dies. His son, Richard Cromwell is unable to maintain the Protectorate and resigns in Spring 1659.

[Click for Timeline: 1660 to 1700](https://www.undiscoveredscotland.co.uk/usfeatures/timeline/to1700.html)
